clue.text: Model soldier given very little money, reportedly

parts.note: a PARA is a paratrooper, a common crossword soldier

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the next word is heard rather than read, so its sound is used

parts.note: a dime is a ten-cent coin, a very small sum

explanation.surface: A model soldier is handed almost no pay, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The last syllable is said like 'dime', the US ten-cent coin, but spelt DIGM.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a pattern or exemplar, which is what a model is.

clue.text: Delay start of pint with posh man about town

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage, meaning posh
a toff is a smartly dressed upper-class man, a man about town

explanation.surface: A drink is put back while a smart socialite joins the round.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off something is to postpone it, a phrasal synonym for delay.

clue.text: Become friends again? Do you mean it?

definitions.meaning: to ally again, read as ..., is to renew a friendship
an exclamation asking whether someone is serious

explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-ally it means renew an alliance; said as one word it is the question 'is that so?'.

clue.text: Desperate-sounding families making impassioned speeches

indicators.note: the suffix -sounding tells us to use how the attached word is said, not its spelling

parts.note: dire means desperate, as in dire straits
tribes are groups of related families

explanation.surface: Families in a bad way produce angry harangues.
explanation.walkthrough: DIA is said like 'dire', meaning desperate.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a speech full of passion.

clue.text: Grow sad and wiser if abandoned? He might

indicators.note: abandoned suggests letters let loose and thrown into disorder, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man left alone might grow sad and become wiser.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of GROW SAD and WISER gives the answer; the question mark invites the whole clue as a picture of him.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass widower is a man whose wife is away, so the abandoned man who might grow sad.

clue.text: Hindu warrior assigned to position by British administration

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece is placed next to the other

parts.note: the Raj was British rule in India
put means placed or assigned to a position

explanation.surface: A Hindu soldier gets posted by the colonial government.
explanation.definitionFit: Rajputs are a Hindu caste traditionally of warriors and rulers.

clue.text: Group of characters caught up in bleak calamity, sadly

indicators.note: caught up in a down clue means the captured letters are read upwards
a group of characters is a string of letters taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dreadful disaster leaves its victims in sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'bleaK CALAmity' backwards gives the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an old interjection of regret, used where we might say sadly or alas.

clue.text: All-seeing God Christian not at first supporting

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

indicators.note: not at first tells us to drop the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a Copt is an Egyptian Christian, so Coptic describes one

explanation.surface: God and a believer combine to watch over all.
explanation.walkthrough: A Coptic is a Christian of the Egyptian church; lose its first letter for OPTIC, which supports PAN in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Panoptic means seeing everything at once, a learned synonym for all-seeing.

clue.text: Checking score, seeing big boy's finish in front of goal

parts.note: tall means big in height

indicators.note: a word's finish is its last letter
front of picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A tall lad scores and someone is keeping count of the goals.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallying is counting up a score, so checking it.

clue.text: Rip off unruly character

parts.note: to tear is to rip
away means off, as in gone off or away

explanation.surface: A hooligan rips something off.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a reckless, wild young person.

clue.text: From grass, learned criminal was giving out ecstasy

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters have gone wrong, so they are rearranged once one is removed

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A grass learned that a criminal was dealing ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange LEARNED and drop one E; 'grass' looks like the informer of the surface but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Darnel is a weedy ryegrass found in cornfields.

clue.text: Honour former editor somehow

indicators.note: somehow signals the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A retired editor is decorated in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Order of Merit is a British honour given by the monarch.

clue.text: Office worker right at the back of the queue

indicators.note: at the back of places one piece after the other

parts.note: a file is a line of people, a queue

explanation.surface: A clerk is standing at the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A filer is someone who files documents, an office job.

clue.text: One's out to obtain such an allowance

definitions.text: One's out to obtain such an allowance

parts.words: One's out to obtain such an allowance
parts.note: a worker who is out on a walkout receives this union payment

explanation.definitionFit: Strike pay is money a trade union pays its members during a strike.

clue.text: Erasure of broadcast educated people appeared on

parts.note: OB stands for outside broadcast
the literati are well-read, educated people
taken as written

explanation.surface: A programme featuring intellectuals gets wiped.
explanation.definitionFit: Obliteration is complete wiping out, so an erasure.

clue.text: Head off from the sea, having captured man from South America

indicators.note: having captured means one piece holds the other inside it
head off from means the first letter is removed

parts.note: marine means of the sea
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A man is seized while heading out to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sea' stands for the adjective marine; 'Head off from' leaves ARINE, and 'having captured' wraps that round the man. 'Argentine' as a noun can also mean the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentine describes someone or something from Argentina in South America.

clue.text: Saintly character brought up to become an American soldier

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the whole run is read upwards

parts.note: suit means to become, as a colour becomes you
GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A saint was raised to join the US army.
explanation.definitionFit: St Ignatius of Loyola founded the Jesuits, a saint.

clue.text: State doctor developed photo for spy

parts.note: MI is the postal abbreviation for Michigan, a US state

indicators.note: developed suggests something worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor develops a picture for a secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developed' reads as film processing but rearranges DOCTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A microdot is a photograph shrunk to a dot, used for hiding secrets in espionage.

clue.text: Arty type wins parliamentary seat, perhaps

parts.note: gains means wins
a borough can be a parliamentary constituency

explanation.surface: An artist wins a seat in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gainsborough was an English portrait and landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainsborough was a famous painter, so an arty type.

clue.text: Having nothing to start with, a Scottish engineer raised capital

indicators.note: to start with puts this piece at the beginning

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish steam engineer

explanation.surface: An engineer from Scotland, starting with nothing, raised funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada.

clue.text: Toast initially put on shelf

indicators.note: on in a down clue places one piece above the other
initially picks the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a ledge is a shelf

explanation.surface: The toast was set out on a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge someone is to drink a toast to them.

clue.text: Current goal is to grasp translation of Sartre

indicators.note: grasp means hold, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: an aim is a goal

indicators.note: translation of means turning the word into a different form, so rearranging it

explanation.surface: The goal is to understand a French philosopher in translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translation of' turns the philosopher's name into RSTREA, and 'is to grasp' has the goal hold it; the surface's French reading is a red herring for the definition 'Current'.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstream is a current of air.

clue.text: Animal can move inside

indicators.note: inside puts one piece within another

parts.note: a tin is a can
a go is a move in a game

explanation.surface: An animal can move about indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is a hybrid of a tiger and a lioness.

clue.text: Concerned with the birth of two boys

parts.note: Nat is a boy's name
Al is another boy's name

explanation.surface: Two boys have to do with a birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is the adjective for birth.

clue.text: Jones kept blond finally using dye

indicators.note: kept means held, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: Inigo Jones was the English architect

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Jones kept his blond look by dyeing it.
explanation.walkthrough: Inigo Jones (1573-1652) was the English architect who designed the Banqueting House.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue dye.

clue.text: Love money?. Racket's involved trainee professional

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up within

parts.note: the rand is South African currency
din means racket, noise

explanation.surface: Love of money and noise involve a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinand is a candidate training for ordination, a trainee clergyman.

clue.text: Installing computers for use in either half of prison

indicators.note: for use in places one piece within the other

parts.note: Sing Sing is the New York prison; either half is the same word
IT is information technology, computers

explanation.surface: Computers are being installed in a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Siting is placing in position, so installing.

clue.text: Passenger accommodation always available in coach

indicators.note: available in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach
e'er is poetic for ever, always

explanation.surface: There is always room for passengers on the coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage is the cheapest passenger accommodation on a ship.
